thread:
kevin: Quick heads up — integration test failing in staging when the client omits x-redwood-project-id. Seems to blow up with a 500 from api-server.
maya: ugh. do you have a minimal repro curl?
kevin: yeah pasted below. Repro is: \n```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_test_abc' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","input":"hi"}'
```
No x-redwood-project-id or x-redwood-org-id headers. Expectation: 401 or 403 with a structured JSON error explaining missing scope. Actual: 500 + stack trace in logs.
jordan: do logs show a nil deref or an assert? that smells like code assuming project meta always present after auth lookup.
sara: confirming — the auth middleware currently tries to resolve project from token metadata and then dereferences project.zones without a fallback. If token->project missing it returns internal error instead of an auth error.
lia: this is a regression from the key-rotation PR (recently merged). That PR added more aggressive metadata caching; edge-case for legacy org-scoped keys slipped.
kevin: propose we map any "missing identity metadata" path to 401 with body: `{ "error": "missing authentication headers or invalid API key" }` and log details for SRE. And explicitly treat org-scoped keys: fallback to org if project header missing, but only if the token's scope allows org fallback.
maya: +1. important to keep backward compat: previously some clients used only x-redwood-org-id. We need tests for both flows.
jordan: quick suggestion for response shape: keep our standard error envelope: `{ "ok": false, "code": "auth_missing_project", "message": "x-redwood-project-id header missing and token not project-scoped" }`. That helps clients programmatically handle it.
sara: agreed on envelope. Also add a specific 401 vs 403 mapping: 401 for "no valid credentials", 403 for "credentials valid but not authorized for requested project". Avoid 500 unless truly internal.
ci-bot: build 7982 started for branch fix/auth-fallback (kevin)
kevin: I pushed a tiny patch that checks for nil before deref and returns standardized error. PTAL: https://git.internal/redwood/repo/pulls/4123
maya: reviewing now. also add an e2e asserting that when project header missing and token is org-scoped we return 200 (if org allows) or 403 if org lacks access.
kevin: good call. For rotation: we should document grace behavior — during rotation keys may be org-scoped then project-scoped. Add a compatibility note in api-contracts.md explaining fallback precedence: 1) explicit x-redwood-project-id header, 2) project associated with key (if present), 3) org fallback if token is org-scoped and org has default project mapping.
jordan: who owns the api-contracts.md section? pinging @sara
sara: I'll take it, will update with examples and an HTTP table (status/code/body).
lia: please also add a QA checklist: - unit: auth middleware maps missing metadata -> 401 - integration: org-only header -> success/403 cases - contract: error envelope names + codes - docs: example curl and sdk behavior
kevin: one more nit — when auth fails we should not leak internal exception details in body. Only log trace ID and high-level message.
maya: agreed. add a short note for SDKs: map auth_missing_project to a dedicated exception type so clients can surface UI prompts.
kevin: thanks. If reviewers sign off I'll merge and roll to staging after CI.
sara: LGTM pending tests. maya can you finish integration tests?
maya: on it. will add tests and follow up here. :thumbsup:
kevin: awesome, thanks everyone.
ci-bot: build 7982 succeeded (unit + lint) — awaiting integration suite results.
maya: integration tests green locally, will push in 5.
kevin: pushed tests and addressed comments. merging now.
lia: note for post-deploy: watch auth-error-rate dashboard for spike and check error codes instead of 500s.
kevin: noted. will monitor and post follow-up if anything odd shows up.
